item.title: A draft featuring the Village People, Shrunken Heads, Neurotoxins and Clickbait: Re: A draft featuring the Village People, Shrunken Heads, Neurotoxins and Clickbait
item.content:encoded: I'm speechless. This draft is utterly ridiculous, not-at-all serious, and a complete joke. And the best comedic scip I've read yet. Seriously, how has no one commented on this? The final log is one of the best things about it. You set up a (semi)realistic scenario with the cops, and then turn everything on its head with a cosmic entity. I only have one real question. Why has the Foundation not attempted to use this to help contain/slow down dangerous scips? Although you definitely have enough material, a short addenda talking about perhaps the results of some tests on other scips could provide a comedic sharp contrast between the incident report and a bit of dry, humorless test results. But yes, I certainly found it lovely to read, and you kept me chuckleing the entire time.

item.title: The Interdimensional Bodega: Re: The Interdimensional Bodega
item.content:encoded:
Placeholder comment, will add in crit in a bit. So far, I like the concept of a non-violent resolution!

Edit:
Line-by-Line:

+ Show
- Hide

SCP-XXXX-1 is to be stationed with a concierge staffed by a Foundation personnel at all times.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but a concierge is a person, so it should be something like "SCP-XXXX-1 is to be staffed at all times by Foundation personnel, with at least one taking on the role of a concierge."

All entrants to SCP-XXXX-1 will allowed one of four choices:

This doesn't have the best clinical tone, I'd phrase it as "Upon entry, all entrants to SCP-XXXX-1 will be presented with a choice of four objects:"

The use of amnestics on entrants is punishable by termination.

Crank that way down. Termination means getting killed, usually, and the effects of amnesticization don't seem deserving of punishment via death.

SCP-XXXX is a symbol visible only to approximately 20% of the population. The reason for this is unknown.

First, scratch that entire second line. It's an anomaly, of course it's unknown. As for the first sentence, it moves too fast and doesn't give enough information. A symbol? What kind? Visible or invisible in what ways?

SCP-XXXX’s location varies, however, the most consistent location on which it is found is any type of featureless wall with high amounts of activity and traffic.

So it moves around? Or is someone drawing it in various places? You gotta explain things more.

Individuals who can see SCP-XXXX are granted access to SCP-XXXX-1; access to SCP-XXXX-1 is done by placing an open hand on SCP-XXXX. The wall on which SCP-XXXX is visible will then dissipate, revealing an entrance to SCP-XXXX-1.

Again, slow down the pacing. It's hard to understand what you mean here, even though you've given enough information.

Clothing themed after the GoI, the Wandsmen.

Hit the brakes. You're introducing an entire new GoI that we know nothing about in a single bullet point, and treating it casually like we're supposed to know everything about them. Also, you'd probably want to state it like "GoI-12345 'The Wandsmen'" or something more clinical.

How they obtained this information

"How this information was obtained"

SCP-XXXX-1’s main retail lobby is managed by PoI-XXXX (need better name later lol) and PoI-XXXX-2, bipedal avian creatures with features similar to owls (Strigiformes) and both standing at approximately 2 meters.

At this point, these two wouldn't be PoIs. They'd be subanomalies, like SCP-XXXX-2A and SCP-XXXX-2B.

- Hide

I'll admit I stopped reading at this point. You very consistently don't give enough information and are lacking clinical tone, to the point where the reader loses interest before they get to the logs. You move along far too quickly to set up any points of reference for the reader, which leads to me being halfway down the article and still feeling lost and confused.

Work on those things, then feel free to message me again to review the full draft.

item.title: Impregnating Ultrasound (Tale): Re: Impregnating Ultrasound (Tale)
item.content:encoded:
I hammered mostly down on all the SPaG stuff and thought I should come back and give some more thorough thoughts on the actual story and pacing.

[+] Open
[-] Close

I already talked enough about the falling action of the Gregory-baby climax, but the rising action into it is also a bit lacking I feel. The rising action where Gregory gets snatched initially I feel you did nicely and it flowed pretty well, but the next one came out of left field completely, there was barely any indication that anything like this was going to happen. Suffice to say, I was not sufficiently mentally prepared for a tiny, middle aged man to come crawling out of a vaginal cavity. I was especially unprepared because of the similarity of this situation to the initial Gregory one where Gregory just simply disappeared and there were no established insane horror elements as of that point.

The introduction to Lisa's plan is perfectly fine, but it came off to me as a bit fast where she comes up with it and then executes it, she doesn't toil over whether or not she should do it before becoming strong in her conviction or whatever. But I would like to compliment you on revealing where the ultra sound machine was moved to, because when it is written that she asks the staff, you don't reveal where it actually is until James and Lisa are there doing the impregnating thing and I really liked that.

In the initial Gregory scenario, where he goes missing, I didn't immediately realize that he had literally disappeared in front of the lady who later birthed him. Consider, after it says Gregory wasn't in the room, mentioning that he hadn't left the room or have the lady remark that he vanished before her eyes.

A lovely day to you as well.

item.title: Impregnating Ultrasound (Tale): Re: Impregnating Ultrasound (Tale)
item.content:encoded:
Here's a tiny smidgen of crit:

[+] Open
[-] Close

The night breeze was cool and dry, unbelievably rare for Florida, even in Winter.

Winter is not a proper noun and as such, shouldn't be capitalized.

She sat back in her car for a moment longer, just one moment longer

This line is fine, but located a paragraph down from that quote is the line, "thinking about his blue, blue eyes" which might come off as repetitive.

Hers were brown. She turned off her car, stepped out and close the door behind her.

Should be "closed." Imo, there's too many "hers" here.

Damned global warming and such.

I personally don't really like the "and such" tacked on at the end.

She walked over to her front door and went through her keys, searching for the one to her house.

Same thing as earlier, so many "hers."

the door clicked open from the other side and slid open

I've never heard of a sliding front door, but that might just be me. Slightly more important crit goes to the use of "open" twice.

she stepped into the house and locked the front door.

You've already stated that this is the front door, no need to do it again.

She rested him on her lap, with him leaning deeply into her belly.

I'd change this around to use "leaned" rather than "leaning" to keep with the past tense, something like, "She rested him on her lap while he leaned deeply into her belly."

she dug her fingernails into his scalp and felt him shiver under her touch. As he always did, every single night.

I'd make this all one sentence, I think you'd just need to remove the period and that'd be it.

"Did you shower yet?" Lisa asked her.

Her kid suddenly switches gender.

He nestled his hair deeply into Lisa's bosom, quickly feeling a second pair of arms wrap around him; the arms of unconsciousness.

I'd change it to "bosom and quickly felt" to keep with the past tense. "The arms of unconsciousness" make it sound like Lisa fell asleep, but it was James that fell asleep? It could also be interpreted that the arms of unconsciousness make people fall asleep, either way, I think it's too vague.

His breath came out tiny, mousy snores.

add "in" after "out."

Lisa felt a tiny smidgen of drool drop on her shoulder.

There's nothing inherently wrong here, but consider removing "tiny" because "smidgen" is already a small amount of something, so you have a "tiny small amount of something."

peered deeply at his peaceful, pale, pudgy face.

Personal opinion, I don't particularly like the use of three adjectives here, especially the fact that they all start with a "p."

She tapped them against the table

I could be wrong here, but I think it's supposed to say "taped" even if it is or isn't it's of a weird thing to do, tapping paper against a table or taping paper against a table just doesn't seem like something people do?

Just then,

You have used this a couple times, consider switching one of them out to avoid repetition.

SIGNATURE: Lisa Goldsman

If you're interested I could show you how to make that into a written signature on the page rather than it just being typed out in the generic font.

Test results from a few years back. Test results for severe chlamydia.

This is the third time you use this kind of purposeful repetition (the first two being "just a moment longer," and "blue, blue eyes") I'd consider changing some of them out to avoid repetition in the repetition.

She allowed herself a slight frown, deadened and dulled by time, folded up the papers and put them back in the drawers.

This is clunky if you say it aloud? It just doesn't feel right for the pacing of a sentence. And why are the papers for her test results stored in multiple different drawers?

And then she crawled into bed and went to sleep.

I think this would work better with descriptors rather than "and then" eg: "Weathered and weary, she crawled into bed and went to sleep."

Lisa pat James on the head and opened the front door

She's multitasking! Patting her kid on the head and opening the door at the same time!

She stepped aside and ushered Sammy inside.

I don't particular like the similarity of "inside" and "aside" being used here, I'd replace "inside" with "into the house" or some such to avoid the repetition.

she picked up the three year old, spun the squealing, smiling three year old

No need to say he's three years old twice.

Lisa waved in response.

This, to me, sounds like Lisa put on her shoes and stood in the hall a couple feet from James and just stood there and waved, she didn't even leave, just stood there and waved for no discernible amount of time. I'd rephrase this to something like, "Lisa waved back to him while strolling out the door."

She did not stop to humor him; she said nothing and walked away.

This is basically the same sentence written twice.

rather concerning for a woman at age twenty-seven

I'm not sure how I feel about the phrasing of "age twenty-seven" but this is good characterization, her age doesn't seem overly forced in here, it's good.

frantically looked around at her colleagues and looked back to the ultrasound room.

More multitasking, she's looking at her colleagues and looking back to the room at the same time, I don't even think that's possible!

looked back to the ultrasound room. She didn't know why she was doing this, but she didn't care.

The second sentence here I believe is supposed to refer to her going to the ultrasound room, but it's stated before she actually does anything and comes off as referring to her looking toward the room.

This time, not with a stiff lip and white knuckled grip; this time, with wide eyes and a confused gaze.

This is that same purposeful repetition, you use it too much!

What the hell is going on…?

I'm not really a fan of the "…?" but that's really just personal preference.

Quick note: I think the anomalous stuff was introduced very smoothly and in a timely manner where her struggles were sufficiently set up and it is still unclear how it'll be of benefit to her, I really like how you managed that.

Until the third trimester.

a few lines after this, you use "until now" and it's a little tiny bit repetitive.

Another quick note: holy fucking shit that was absolutely terrifyingly brilliant and horrifying, I think you leave just enough details vague that the reader fills in the blanks and it is fucking well done. The only criticism that I have on that part is that the falling action feels like it plummets and then ends a bit quick.

And ran. And drove

These two lines together like that sound a bit off, perhaps she runs all the way home and has to go back for her car later? I just really don't like the "and drove" bit.

Nobody could.

I really like that line, it adds a lot for being so short.

St. Mary's Hospital.

If that's the one in PA, I've been there (toddler-me smashed his dumbass head into a wall.)

Lisa caressed his brown little curls and little scratched a nail down his forehead and bridge of his nose, earning a little giggle from him.

Little, little, little. Also, I'm not sure what "little scratched a nail down his forehead" means? I think it's a mistake?

his pudgy little smile

This is the second time you call him "pudgy."

closely examining every wrinkle on her face.

Correct me if I am wrong, but earlier she said she didn't care about her wrinkles and this moment shows her becoming more concerned about such things and it is great characterization, which is something that is exuded by this tale.

Her gaze slowly shifted to her belly

The paragraph that starts with this sentence is a great paragraph, my only issue with it is that you use the word "belly" three times.

She gazed at his curly sandy hair

This is the second time you call his hair "curly sandy." I had some previous crit on the first use of it because I didn't realize that sandy was the color of his hair and I thought that his hair actually had sand in it. Consider clearing that up because I don't think "sandy" is generally immediately associated with the color of sand and rather something having sand in it.

This was what she wanted, even if James didn't. But he'd make her want it.

I believe these are contradictory statements, James doesn't want it, James will make her want it.

I was about to critique the word "quiet" because I thought you spelled it wrong, but it was just a bit of jamais vu and I'm an idiot.

"Okay!" James whispered loudly.

This is a nice touch.

The next three trimesters would be lonely, but oh, so worth it.

I'd remove the comma after "oh."

The first month was lonely. Oh, so lonely.

This is yet another example of the purposeful repetition. Also this line is a single line below a line that also has the "oh," line in it.

Lisa awakened in the middle of the night to forceful contractions.

It feels like it has only been one month, since the marker for one month was directly stated while none others were. I think you could do well to remove any mention of time passing entirely in this segment to not set expectations for the reader.

And she didn't need the hospital.

Starting here, the next eight lines start with, or nearly start with the word "she."

one that could only be made by a hyena hyped up on crack cocaine.

This is a fun descriptor, but it breaks immersion severely. I strongly suggest finding something less comical to compare her laugh to.

'you hate me! I hate you! I hate you, Lisa!'

I could be wrong here, but shouldn't these be quotation marks?

"What?!"

Personal preference, I don't really like the combining of "?" and "!" consider just saying "'What?'"

His hair was still curly, but it was now the same bright shade of blonde as her hair. He opened his eyes and they were no longer that hideous blue, but an identical shade of brown to hers.

This is a good line, it lets readers remember the times you explicitly stated their different hair color and eye color, a good little "ohhhh" moment.

The final line is satisfying and would clear up any confusion on the part of the reader toward how the relationships between all of the people worked.

I mentioned before, the falling action after Gregory comes crawling out feels like dropping a stone and it ends quite quickly too.

Despite all I had to say about it, I think you wrote a horrifying story with great characterization, foreshadowing, setup and all that and it was very enjoyable to read. Just watch out for all that repetition I mentioned and polish it up a bit.

his newborn mouth still full of baby teeth.

Oh my God it's a newborn talking with a full set of baby teeth, why do you have to conjure these images?

item.title: Shepherd boy (working title): Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

This doesn't have enough 'conflict' driving the story forwards: everyone feels like a passive observer at best, and there's not really anything pulling this forwards. It doesn't help that the various elements feel…disconnected?

Like, the exploration log doesn't smoothly lead into the interview because there's nothing really tying the exploration into the idea of the division between two church groups and that whole conflict; the two things feel completely separate thematically, particularly since the role of the snake and the yurt and stuff is just…completely irrelevant to the interview with -1 and the discovery that there's some spooky churches behind this and there's like…two sets of people and stuff? It feels like this just, doesn't tie all the elements involved in this together well enough, or do much with anything and it's underwhelming as a result.

I would strongly suggest trimming down the concept: figure out what stuff is actually necessary, and get rid of all the unnecessary anomalous stuff. Like, you have this dude who's meant to be able to shape earth but that never actually comes up in this, so cut that aspect. You have the giant snake, but it's not really a major element so cut it from the description. You have the dude manifesting anomalies and talk of this spreading further, but none of that comes up so cut it. Be ruthless: anything that does not serve either the characterisation, the narrative or the emotional response here is unnecessary. Equally: any narrative thread that doesn't go anywhere is unnecessary; any characterisation that isn't purposeful is unnecessary.

This, at it's core, needs a central thing holding it up: an idea, or a theme; and it needs to figure out how to introduce that theme early and expand on it, and explore it throughout. Everything should serve the central core of this: the exploration should introduce it, the interview should expand it, and the note at the end should resolve it.

In it's current state, I would downvote this. I…am not confident that a version of this exists that I would upvote without you effectively starting from scratch on a more streamlined article.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

is to be kept in a standard humanoid cell and itwhich should be suspended in mid-air

with height measuring 300m from the sea level

this phrasing implies exactly 300m; "at least 300m above" would be clearer than "with height measuring 300m from"

It feels to me like measuring it from sea level is a mistake: you want to convey that it's 300m from the ground, which isn't necessarily sea level.

Four wires are to be installed on all four sides to keep the cell stable.

I think the exact details of the suspension can be elided; with the sole exception being if we need to understand this to know how a containment breach or something occurred.

It is to be noted that all carbon-based life areis prohibited to enterfrom entering SCP-XXXX-1’s containment cell.

'carbon-based life' feels clunky here; I feel like 'personnel' is sufficient but?

a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures asto SCP-XXXX-1.

A maximum of five hazmat-protected personnel isare permitted to enter SCP-XXXX at any given time.

Five personnel is plural; so are instead of is.

all on-site personnel isare to evacuate or shelter in place until MTF-Theta-4 ("Gardeners") apprehend SCP-XXXX-1 and its anomalies manifestation.

I think you want 'anomalous manifestations' here?

Description:

I'd get rid of the horizontal line immediately after this; though tbh, I'd generally lean to keeping the description and the first sentence of the description on the same line.

SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX

This is janky: you can't assign 'SCP-XXXX' to both 'the overall' and 'the cave' like this.

the abandoned Mining facility

mining shouldn't be capitalised here or anywhere in sentences like this.

in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia

in the ConProcs, you refer to it as "located in Altai Tavan Bogd, Mongolia"; and it feels like you should be consistent here?

it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

It's unclear whether this refers to the cave or the mine; I'd move the measurement depending on which:

SCP-XXXX is a 6km deep cave under the abandoned mining facility in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia.

or:

SCP-XXXX is a cave under the 6km deep abandoned mining facility in Tavan Bogd, Mongolia.

This also prevents the kinda janky two clauses joined by a comma structure.

at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave

this feels really big in relation to the cave depth but? I guess it works if the cave is largely horizontal rather than vertical? It might be worth specifying an area the cave system takes up

Within SCP-XXXX are groups of humanoid entities stationary in place, their physical traits are as same as humans but is made out of a roots that is growing a different species of flowers, those flowers are identical to the organism above the surface and is emitting unknown amount of pollen.

This is a really long run on sentence that really needs to be two sentences at least.

'physical traits' to me implies 'they move like people', I think 'physical appearance' might be what you're aiming for? Or alternatively to just say 'humanoid entities that are stationary and made out of roots'.

'stationary in place' is redundant: one implies the other.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'organism above the surface', unless you mean 'identical to non-anomalous flowers'?

The pollen seemed to affectaffects the mind of a subjects who entered the proximity of the humanoids.

'seemed' is an unnecessary cop out; and the rest is a tense change to make it read better.

When inhaled the pollen

"When the pollen is inhaled,"

It is unknown what will happen after the symptoms as it is yet to be recorded.

This is weird phrasing because it kinda implies the foundation like, were taking notes of someone being affected, and then like…stopped after a while and then didn't note down what else happened.

"The long term effects of exposure are currently unknown." would be a better way to phrase this idea.

Similar to the humanoids, SCP-XXXX has an ecosystem made entirely out of carbon-based life and is being inhabitant by an animals that is identical to animals above the cave, however, the animals are made out of the same components as their surroundings, particularly different species of woods, plants, etc.

This is another huge run on sentence that really needs broken into smaller parts.
'an ecosystem made entirely out of carbon-based life' is unnecessary and can be cut; same for 'similar to the humanoids': just be like 'SCP-XXXX is inhabited by animals composed of plant matter, which are analogous to non-anomalous animals'. Specifying 'woods, plants, etc.' basically conveys nothing.

Footnote 2: It is noted that there’s no soft substance of a human or other animal body, consisting of muscle and fat are present inside of SCP-XXXX.

'It is noted that there's no substance resembling soft tissue, such as muscle and fat, present inside SCP-XXXX'

It is speculated that these animals have grown out of nature and started to inhabit the area, however it is yet to be proven.

I would cut this because it's just, unnecessarily vague. Perhaps saying 'It is speculated that these animals have evolved naturally' would work but?

During substantial viewing of SCP-XXXX, it was apparent that the biome inside of SCP-XXXX is contagious to the outside world.

This is weird; it doesn't work for me at all and I think it's the way the information is being presented. Something like:

The biome within SCP-XXXX is capable of spreading outside the cave system

would be clearer; but it'd raise questions of why the ConProcs don't really have anything to stop the spread beyond 'arrest stuff leaving the cave'.

It's also unclear what you mean by 'biome' since the only life you've referred to so far is plants making up people/animals, whereas this sounds like you're referring to like…plant life?

3 months after SCP-XXXX’s discovery the biome has spread about 7m outside of the cave. Causing the containment of the area to expand along with it.

These should be the same sentence.

Currently, there’s no way of stopping it.

'there is'

Its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and deteriorating, physically it looks as if it in its mid-teens but its age is currently unknown.

This is janky as hell too; something like "Its skin is olive brown from sun damage; physically it appears to be in its mid-teens though the actual age of SCP-XXXX-1 is unknown." might read better but it feels a little like this should perhaps be two sentences?

made entirely out of organic material.

'organic material' is entirely too vague: 'plant matter' would be better if that's what you're aiming for? Otherwise the assumption is 'blood and flesh' and then you just have a normal dragon, y'know?

Entities length is unknown.

I'm not a fan of this sentence or the information it conveys: it feels like something like "The entity is estimated to be [30-50m] long" would be clearer; with the size varied depending on your idea of how big this is.

With indeterminate means, SCP-XXXX-1 can manipulate any carbon-based life for its disposal, this includes causing earthquakes and using it's surroundings as a weapons through telekinesis.

I'd cut the 'With indeterminate means,' here; it feels like it's better to just say what it can do and not specify how.

Footnote 3 is also unnecessary and I'd cut it.

Though it is studied that SCP-XXXX-1, when unresponsive, will still exhibit its anomalous ability and affect the surrounding air, causing asphyxiation on the subject closer to SCP-XXXX-1’s unconscious body.

Consider:

SCP-XXXX-1, when unconscious, will still exhibit anomalous properties which can affect the surrounding air and cause asphyxiation in nearby subjects.

'nearby' feels vague; but I think it's better than specifying it. Though, to be honest, introducing yet more anomalous properties here feels like a mistake: IMO the abilities of -1 need trimmed to one thing it can do.

SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1 were discovered byduring a series of civilian interviews in Altai Tavan Bogd, Mongolia in █/██/2020

I'd unredact this date fully: the date isn't sensitive information; particularly not more sensitive than what this SCP can do.

deployed in to explore the cave and return with the sample

'with the sample' is still really janky even with a footnote explaining what you mean: I would honestly just say they were deployed to explore the cave and leave it at that.

After they had not returned 24 hours later, a recovery team was dispatched to investigate, only the non-organic components of MTF Zeta-9's equipment were found.

I would probably cut this? Idk, it feels like opening with 'we didn't find Zeta-9' undercuts a lot of the tension of the log because we know it turns out badly?

Maybe it'd work better noted at the end?

Agent Olson: got it.

Missing capital

Agent Olson: Currently… nothing.

It's unclear if Olson means 'We have no ideas about what the cave does' or 'This cave does nothing'

Agent Ouyulan: Then how are we going to travel through this anyway?

There's nothing to indicate there'd be difficulty travelling through this yet.

any of you heard anything?

Shit! why did it get dark? everyone flashlight on!

This is weird cos there's been no indication it got dark before this?

The snake lunges at Agent Ouyulan, but she opens fire on the creature, however it doesn't seemed to be affected.

'but' here implies 'the gun fire prevents the lunge', which the 'however it doesn't seem to be affected' directly contradicts.

During its rampage, its tail hits Agent Olson sendingwhich sends him flying.

The snake is seen swallowing Agent Zachary whole

you need to establish the scale of the snake before this: the implication from 'a snake skeleton' is 'snake sized' whereas 'swallows a man whole' implies 'much larger'.

Well shit, guess we're alone, are we?

Yeah, let us stick together. Don't wander off somewhere else alone. Let's get going.

These are highly trained professionals. Wandering off alone is like…the last thing they should expect the other to do.

The camera activates, the date on the feed tellsindicates its been five hours since the snake attack.

Frantic panting can be heard behind the camera as Agent Olson is seen running through a narrow tunnel,with a bright light can be seen inat the end of it.

The three agents finally reaches a wide space.

'finally' implies the passage of time but cos it's not really shown, it feels weird? Maybe 'After an hour, the three agents reach a wide space' would be better?

found jack shit and now we're in a completely different place.

Agent Olson starts to look around the area, picking up a rock and peddle, feeling the walls of the cave, the camera went static for three minutes and Agent Olson is sitting crossed leg, facing the wall.

Run on sentence

Also I think you mean 'pebble'? But it's weird for Olson to pickup a rock and then not do anything with it: maybe indicate they put it in a sample bag and store it in their rucksack or something?

Is it me or is the air is less timid than when we started?

'timid' is still not the word you're looking for here. I think you want 'thin' maybe?

(a fore)

I think this should really be like 'from off-camera' or something?

drink this, it might help.

It seems like something is messing with frame.

'frame' isn't the right word here: I think maybe 'with the signal' or something but??

No need for messingto mess with that thing

Agent Luna: Umm Cap!

This is the only place anyone is referred to as 'Cap': I would use the more familiar designation.

They all are human.

'human' feels strong here; 'They are all human' would be more grammatically correct but 'They all look like people' might be clearer?

The feet of the crowds embedded into the flower field.

Saying this implies 'the feet are suddenly embedded into…' whereas I think you're really trying to convey that they always were: maybe highlighting someone looking down and noticing it or something would work better?

it seems like these people were on a run?

The description does not imply this to be the case so it feels like a jarring suggestion.

//Agent Olson was silent/

Missing a / at the end

facilities in a three-decade span.

The hyphen is unnecessary too

You caused thousands of deaths.

Hence why you're here.

This isn't actually why -1 is here; -1 is here because he's anomalous and the foundation locks up anomalies; they don't really care about regular humans who kill folk.

SCP-CXXX-1: Will you let me go if I answer? I need to go to my people.

'CXXX' should be 'XXXX'

But I won’t promise you to answer everything.

'But I won't promise I'll answer everything.'

To be honest I can't quite tell you… I never opened it before.

This implies "-1 doesn't know", which it's weird for Kent to follow with 'You can tell me'.

Dr. Kent: Why?

This feels like it should be "How?" as in "How were your peoples existence threatened"

When i was a child, there was a two division of belief, and our people belong in none of those division.

I'm not sure what you mean by 'division of belief'

This whole paragraph feels…very expositional? In like, a bad way: it's just dumping a lot of info in our lap without really giving us a reason to care about the conflict.

first generations to havebe in touch with their inner self.

Did you made them turn them into a tree like your people?
